headline: Strong projects, needs measurable impact
summary: A solid early-career CS resume with relevant AI and cloud projects and a clear technical skills section. Most bullets describe tasks rather than results, which makes the projects feel less impressive than they likely are.

categories.name: Impact & metrics
categories.note: Almost no numbers: users, time saved, accuracy or scale are missing.

categories.name: Clarity & structure
categories.note: Clean one-page layout with standard, easy-to-scan sections.

categories.name: Technical skills
categories.note: Good breadth across Python, React, AWS and Docker.

categories.name: Projects
categories.note: Relevant AI projects, but no links to code or demos.

categories.name: Experience relevance
categories.note: Work history is retail; the transferable skills are framed reasonably well.

categories.name: ATS-friendliness
categories.note: Simple formatting and standard headings parse cleanly.

strengths: Projects use current, in-demand tools (LLMs, FastAPI, Docker, GitHub Actions, AWS)
Clean, single-column format that applicant tracking systems read easily
Retail bullets connect customer communication to client-facing tech work
Clear graduation date and degree concentration

issues.issue: Project bullets have no results or numbers
issues.fix: Add one measurable outcome per project, e.g. how many resumes scanned, build failures analyzed, or minutes saved.

issues.issue: No links to GitHub or live demos
issues.fix: Add a GitHub link in the header and a short link next to each project title.

issues.issue: Objective mentions embedded systems, but most projects are AI/web
issues.fix: Tailor the objective to the role, or cut it and let the projects speak.

issues.issue: Tools line lists basics like Word and IDLE
issues.fix: Drop them to make room for stronger keywords such as PostgreSQL or REST APIs.

issues.issue: Operations Manager role has no dates
issues.fix: Add a date range so the timeline is clear.
